name: snowshoe trail
label: beodeul_city/wave-places/ice-age-field/snowshoe_trail
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

surfaces.part: snowshoe footprint decals (six pale-blue oval prints with small flick marks)

answer.evidence: The drawing is a set of flat oval footprint decals on the ground, seen from above. The silhouette widens to 26 px at row 9 and narrows again to 3 px at row 15. Its shading runs from mid-blue at the top to light blue, then white at the bottom. This is a highlight gradient, not a vertical face: there is no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no separate front face of 3 or more rows. It has no standing volume, so it reads as a flat decal, which matches the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is not a 4x3 ground patch. It is a few small pale-blue snowshoe-print blobs scattered across a flat dark slate background, and the area is smaller than one full tile. The measured tones per tile are 0 for that reason, so I judged by eye. The candidate has only 4 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving. There are about 2 lightness steps on the prints (a pale blue and a slightly darker blue) and no ramp on the background. The background is one flat colour with no grain, speckle or tufts, whereas the grass reference shows several greens in clumps and the paving shows shaded stones. There is no ground surface to judge for texture or outline. This is a sparse set of sprites rather than a surface, so it looks much thinner and flatter than either reference and does not meet the Beodeul bar.

There is no front face of 3 or more rows, no eave shadow and no side face. This is a flat ground decal seen from above, as the 'flat' kind expects.

There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no vertical face of 3 or more rows. The white lower edge reads as a highlight, not a front face. The result is a flat top-down plate, which suits the flat kind.
